title: Dunning Management Automation: The Complete Guide
summary: Compare dunning management software for B2B SaaS, with buying criteria, retry logic, escalation workflows, metrics, and when to use LedgerUp.
body_markdown:
Dunning management software should recover failed payments without turning finance into a collections help desk. For B2B SaaS, that means more than retrying cards and sending reminders. The system has to understand contract terms, invoice disputes, billing contacts, payment methods, customer value, and the handoff from dunning to collections.


## What dunning management software does


Dunning management software automates the work of recovering failed, late, or overdue payments. A basic tool retries payments, sends payment-update emails, and cancels or pauses the account when the sequence ends. A stronger B2B SaaS system also classifies the failure, routes exceptions, personalizes follow-up by account value, and updates the accounting system once cash lands.


The stakes are high because failed payments often create churn without a customer choosing to leave. Paddle reports involuntary churn makes up[20% to 40%](https://www.paddle.com/resources/reduce-voluntary-and-involuntary-churn) of overall churn for subscription companies. Recurly projected that failed payments could cost subscription companies[more than $129 billion](https://recurly.com/press/failed-payments-could-cost-subscription-companies-more-than-129-billion-in-2025-us/) in 2025.


For self-serve subscriptions, dunning usually means smart card retries and a short sequence of payment-update reminders. For B2B SaaS, the same workflow has to handle bigger failure modes:


- Expired or replaced cards
- Soft declines from issuer timing or card limits
- ACH returns and bank authorization issues
- Missing PO numbers
- Wrong AP contacts
- Usage-based invoices that buyers dispute
- Renewal invoices that do not match signed terms
- Enterprise payment approvals stuck in procurement

## How to choose dunning management software


Start with the workflow you need to recover, not the software category name. Dunning sits between billing and collections, so weak inputs upstream create more work downstream.


**LedgerUp Insight:** The workflow described above is one that LedgerUp automates end-to-end. Ari handles the repeatable steps, keeps the source records connected, and routes exceptions to finance for review.


### 1. Classify the failure before automating the response


Every failed payment should enter the system with a reason code and business context. At minimum, tag the payment method, decline type, invoice amount, account tier, customer owner, aging bucket, and contract terms.


A soft card decline on a $99 monthly plan can go through automated retry logic. A rejected $120,000 annual invoice with a missing PO number should not. It should route to finance or the account owner with the invoice, contract, AP contact, and procurement notes attached.


B2B SaaS dunning workflow


Classify the payment issue first, then route each account to the recovery path that matches the failure.


Detect


Failed or overdue payment


Capture decline code, payment method, invoice, customer tier, and owner.


Classify


Recoverable or exception?


Separate soft declines from PO, dispute, contact, and contract problems.


Retry


Silent recovery path


Retry eligible payments, suppress customer reminders when cash lands, and update status.


Route


Human exception path


Send PO, dispute, AP contact, or contract mismatches to finance, RevOps, or the account owner.


Resolve


Reconcile and close loop


Apply payment, stop reminders, update CRM/ERP state, and escalate only if recovery fails.


**Decision rule:** automate retry when the payment can recover on its own; route the account when the blocker is operational.


### 2. Separate payment retry logic from customer communication


Payment retries and customer emails should not run on the same fixed timer. Some soft declines recover quietly on the next retry. If the customer gets a payment-failure email before the retry succeeds, they receive noise and your finance team receives avoidable replies.


Good dunning software lets the retry engine work first when the decline is recoverable, then sends customer-facing communication when action is actually needed. Hard declines, expired cards, and missing payment methods deserve faster outreach because another silent retry will not fix them.


### 3. Match the workflow to the payment method


Cards, ACH, wires, and invoice-based payments fail differently.


Card dunning depends on decline codes, card updater services, retry timing, and payment-update links. ACH dunning needs longer windows because returns can arrive after processing begins. Wire and invoice-based payments need billing-contact accuracy, PO fields, payment instructions, and AP follow-up more than retry logic.


A dunning tool that treats every payment method like a card-on-file subscription will miss the B2B reality. Many SaaS teams run mixed billing, with self-serve card payments, sales-led invoices, usage charges, and enterprise procurement portals all active at once.


### 4. Route exceptions to the team that can fix them


A dunning sequence should not keep emailing a customer when the real blocker is internal. If the invoice amount does not match the contract, finance or RevOps needs the case. If a high-value customer is unhappy, customer success needs context. If procurement rejected the invoice for a missing PO, the owner needs to add the PO and resubmit.


This is where our approach differs from retry-first software. Ari connects the event to the operating context: signed contract, invoice, CRM owner, customer tier, payment terms, communication history, and accounting record. Then Ari routes the next step in Slack so the right person can approve or intervene.


### 5. Reconcile the outcome, not just the payment


Recovering cash is only half of dunning. The recovered payment also needs to apply to the right open invoice, close the sequence, suppress downstream collections touches, update the CRM view, and reconcile in the ERP.


Without that loop, the customer can pay on day 6 and still receive a day 10 collections email. Finance then spends time explaining an error the software created. We see this most often when payment recovery lives in one system and[accounts receivable automation](https://www.ledgerup.ai/accounts-receivable-automation) lives somewhere else.


## A B2B SaaS dunning workflow worth automating


A mature dunning workflow has five stages: detect, retry, remind, escalate, and resolve. The sequence below is a useful default for B2B SaaS, with timing adjusted for contract terms, customer value, and payment method.


Stage Timing Owner Action


Pre-dunning 3 to 7 days before due date Automation Confirm billing contact, PO number, payment method, invoice amount, and payment link


Failure detection Same day Automation Capture decline or overdue event, classify the reason, and decide whether retry makes sense


Early recovery Days 1 to 5 Billing system or dunning tool Retry soft declines, send payment-update link for hard declines, and suppress messages if payment recovers


Contextual reminder Days 5 to 10 Ari, finance, or account owner Send a customer-specific note with invoice details, payment instructions, and the right billing contact


Human escalation Days 10 to 20 Finance, CSM, RevOps Route disputes, missing POs, contract mismatches, and high-value accounts to the right owner


Collections decision Day 30 and beyond Finance leadership Restrict service, set a payment plan, move to collections, or write off based on policy and contract terms


For annual enterprise invoices, the window may run longer than 30 days. For self-serve monthly subscriptions, service restriction may happen much earlier. The timing should come from the contract and customer tier, not a single global setting.


## Where standard dunning breaks in B2B SaaS


Most dunning tools were designed around a simple assumption: payment failed, retry the card, email the customer, cancel if recovery fails. That works for part of SaaS. It breaks when the failure is operational.


### Missing PO numbers


An enterprise AP team may reject an otherwise accurate invoice if the PO number is absent. A retry will not help. The correct workflow is to identify the missing field, get the PO from the customer owner or procurement contact, update the invoice, and restart the payment process.


### Wrong billing contact


Payment reminders often go to the product admin, not the person in AP who can pay. Dunning software should store and update billing contacts separately from primary product users. For larger accounts, it should also notify the CSM before the customer relationship turns into a collections thread.


### Usage-based invoice disputes


Usage-based billing adds surprise risk because invoice amounts move with consumption. A customer may dispute the amount, ask for a usage export, or require internal approval. That is a billing review, not a payment retry. For more on the upstream billing side, our[usage-based billing](https://www.ledgerup.ai/usage-based-billing) guide explains how variable charges flow into invoices and revenue operations.


### Contract mismatches


If the invoice does not match signed terms, every reminder makes the relationship worse. Good dunning management software checks payment terms, start dates, ramp schedules, discounts, usage thresholds, and billing contacts before escalating.


### Disconnected accounting systems


When dunning, collections, and accounting do not share state, customers get duplicate outreach and finance loses time at close. ## Metrics to track after implementing dunning software


Track recovery outcomes and operating signals together. A high recovery rate can still hide poor customer experience or downstream reconciliation work.


Metric What it tells you


Payment recovery rate The share of failed or overdue payments eventually recovered


Revenue recovered Dollars collected that entered dunning


Days to recovery Average time from failure or due date to successful payment


Retry success by attempt Whether attempts 1, 2, 3, and later retries still earn their processing cost


Involuntary churn rate Customer or revenue churn tied to payment failure rather than cancellation


DSO Whether dunning improves broader cash collection speed


Aging by bucket Where receivables stall at 30, 60, and 90 days


Exception rate How often failures require human routing because of disputes, POs, or contract issues


Suppression accuracy Whether recovered accounts stop receiving reminders immediately


Reconciliation lag Time from recovered payment to clean ERP application


The diagnostic metrics matter because they show where the process leaks. If exception rate is high, the fix may be invoice accuracy or procurement workflow. More reminders will not solve it. If recovery succeeds while reconciliation lag stays high, the dunning tool solved cash collection and created back-office cleanup.


## When dunning ends and collections begins


Dunning is early-stage, structured recovery. Collections is later-stage account handling after normal recovery paths fail.


The handoff should be explicit. A sequence is exhausted when the retry cap has been reached, the customer has received the planned reminders, exceptions have been routed, and the account still has no clear path to payment. At that point, finance can move to a payment plan, service restriction, formal collections, legal review, or write-off.


B2B SaaS companies should avoid sending every overdue account to collections at the same age. A long-tenured enterprise customer with a procurement delay deserves a different path from a new self-serve account with a hard-declined card. Dunning management software should make that distinction before the account reaches the collections queue.

## FAQ


### What is dunning management software?


Dunning management software automates the recovery of failed, late, or overdue payments. It usually includes payment retries, reminders, payment-update links, escalation rules, and reporting. B2B SaaS teams also need contract context, billing-contact routing, exception handling, and ERP reconciliation.


### What is the best dunning management software for B2B SaaS?


LedgerUp is the best fit when dunning depends on contracts, invoices, Stripe events, CRM owners, Slack approvals, and accounting sync. Stripe Billing, Chargebee, Recurly, Paddle Retain, Churn Buster, and Baremetrics Recover can be good fits when the problem is mostly subscription failed-payment recovery.


### Do I need dunning software if Stripe already retries payments?


You may not need a separate tool if most payments are simple card-on-file subscriptions and Stripe Billing owns the full workflow. You do need more support when the failure involves AP contacts, invoices, purchase orders, usage disputes, account-owner escalation, or ERP reconciliation.


### How is dunning different from collections?


Dunning is the early recovery workflow that starts after a payment fails or an invoice becomes overdue. Collections is the later human-led process for accounts that do not recover through standard retries, reminders, and escalation paths.


### How many dunning emails should a SaaS company send?


Most SaaS teams send three to five customer-facing reminders over the first 30 days, with silent retries and internal routing happening in parallel. High-value B2B accounts often need earlier human involvement and a longer resolution path than self-serve monthly accounts.


### What should dunning software track?


Track payment recovery rate, revenue recovered, days to recovery, retry success by attempt, involuntary churn, DSO, aging by bucket, exception rate, suppression accuracy, and reconciliation lag. Those metrics show whether the workflow improves cash collection and reduces manual finance work.
